chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud together, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Fazalah ibn Ayub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He was asked about the pregnant woman who sees blood, should she leave the prayer? So he said: Yes, for the pregnant woman sometimes throws out the blood.
ai.seo_question: Does a pregnant woman stop praying if she sees blood?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a pregnant woman experiencing bleeding must suspend her daily prayers, establishing that such bleeding is treated as a state of major ritual impurity (*hadath akbar*) requiring prayer cessation. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that irregular bleeding in pregnancy is not merely physiological but carries specific legal consequences for worship, distinguishing it from regular menstruation (*hayd*) while maintaining the obligation to refrain from *salat* until purity is restored.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Abu Dawood, altogether from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, and Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having been asked about the pregnant woman seeing the blood, ‘Should she leave the Salaat?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes. Sometimes the pregnant woman does tend to throw out the blood’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and Abu Dawud all from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Fadalah ibn Ayyub who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about a pregnant woman who experiences blood discharge whether she must stop performing Salah (prayer)?
He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, she must stop performing Salah (prayer). Sometimes pregnant women also discharge blood.’”
